messages.content: i got up before everyone else today and had tea by the window. i liked not having to talk right away.
it sounds like you enjoyed having a little quiet time before the house was busy.
i do not want to wake early every day. today it just happened.
then it can stay as something you enjoyed today. you do not have to make it a rule for every morning.
can you help me tell my mother why i was quiet when she came in?
i enjoyed a quiet morning by the window. i wanted a little time before talking.
can you make that one sentence?
i enjoyed having some quiet time by the window before talking this morning.
now make it sound like i am ready to talk.
i enjoyed some quiet time by the window this morning. i am ready to talk now.
why is am ready different from was ready?
am ready is about now. was ready is about a time before now.
use both in a message about the same morning.
i was ready for a quiet morning, and now i am ready to talk.
what is the difference between the table is too small and the table is small enough?
too small says the size is a problem for what you want. small enough says the size works for some need, such as putting the table in a small room.
can the same table be too small for dinner but small enough for the room?
yes. those are different needs. a table may go into the room without taking too much space, but not have enough space for everyone to eat.
write that in two simple sentences.
the table is small enough for the room. it is too small for all of us to eat at together.
what if it has room for only two people, and we are two?
then it may be large enough for your meal. whether it is too small changes with how much space you need.
can i say it is enough small?
use small enough. enough comes after small in that sentence.
now use warm instead of small.
the room is warm enough for us to sit here.
make it too warm.
the room is too warm for us to sit here.
does too warm mean everyone in the world would feel the same?
no. it says the room is more warm than works for the people or task being talked about. another person might feel different.
write a story about a neighbor who wants to help in a garden but first asks what is needed.

a woman saw her neighbor working in the garden with a container of water. she wanted to help, so she asked whether any plants needed water. her neighbor said that most had already had enough, but the small plant near the wall still needed some. she gave water to that one, then put the container back. if she had given water to every plant without asking, she might have done work that was not needed. instead, her question helped her use the little time she had where it was useful.
why did she ask before giving water?
she did not know which plants had already had water. her neighbor knew more about what had been done.
did her wish to help give enough information to choose the right task?
no. her wish to help did not tell her which work was needed. asking gave her that information.
write her first question in her voice.
would you like help with the plants? which one needs water?
now make the answer from the neighbor.
thank you. the small plant near the wall needs water. the other plants have had enough for now.
can you finish the story with her having only a few minutes?
she told her neighbor she had only a few minutes before leaving. he said that giving water to the small plant was enough help for that morning. she finished it and went home.
does that make her help less useful because it was short?
no. a short task can be useful when it answers a real need.
my mother, my father, and i need chairs. my parents are coming too. how many different people am i talking about?
you are talking about three people if my parents is about the same mother and father you already gave. saying my parents again does not add two new people.
that is what i mean. now my aunt comes too.
then there are four people: you, your mother, your father, and your aunt.
we have three chairs and one sofa. do we have four chairs?
no. you have three chairs and one sofa. the sofa may give someone a place to sit, but it is not another chair.
can you know everyone has a place to sit?
if the sofa can be used and has space for one person, then yes. three people could use the chairs and one could sit on the sofa.
now i say the sofa is full of books and cannot be used.
then only the three chairs can be used from what you gave, so one of the four people would need another place to sit.
make that explanation shorter.
four people need a place to sit, but only three chairs can be used. one person still needs a place.
if i move the books off the sofa, how many chairs are there?
still three chairs. moving the books can make the sofa useful, but it does not change the number of chairs.
my friend asked whether i am home and whether i can talk. i am home but cannot talk now. write a clear reply.
i am home, but i cannot talk right now.
can you add that i can talk after dinner?
i am home, but i cannot talk right now. i can talk after dinner.
what if i do not know whether i can talk after dinner?
then do not give that as a sure plan. you could say: i am home, but i cannot talk right now. i will let you know if i can talk later.
now only answer the question about being home.
yes, i am home.
why leave out the talk part?
you asked me to answer only the question about being home in that reply. the short answer gives just that information.
could the friend still think i am free to talk because i am home?
they might, so answering both questions is more useful if you want them to know you cannot talk. being home and being free to talk are different facts.
then give the full reply without a plan for later.
i am home, but i cannot talk right now.
write a story about a family looking at an old photo and not knowing one detail.

a family found an old photo while cleaning a shelf. it showed their grandfather near a tree, holding a book. everyone could see the book, but nobody knew what he had been reading. one child said it might be a story. another thought it might be about plants because of the tree. their mother said the tree did not tell them what was in the book. they wrote down what they knew about the photo and left the book question open. later, they could ask their grandfather instead of choosing an answer from the picture alone.
what could they see for sure in the photo?
their grandfather was near a tree and holding a book.
why did the tree not tell them what he was reading?
a person can read many different books near a tree. the place does not give the words inside the book.
can they still enjoy talking about possible stories?
yes, if they keep those ideas as possible stories rather than known facts about the photo.
say that more simply.
they can make up ideas, but should not say those ideas are facts they know.
what question could they ask him?
do you remember what book you were reading in this photo?
what if he does not remember either?
then they do not have to choose an answer. they can still keep and enjoy the photo without knowing every detail.
join these ideas with because: i took a break. i was tired.
i took a break because i was tired.
now use so instead.
i was tired, so i took a break.
why did you change the order?
in your first sentence, the part after because gives the reason you took the break. in the sentence with so, the tired feeling comes first and the break comes after it as what you did.
can i start the because sentence with the reason?
yes. because i was tired, i took a break.
does that change why i took the break?
no. it keeps the same reason and puts it first.
now make it about my brother without changing the reason.
because my brother was tired, he took a break.
can i say because he took a break, he was tired and mean the same thing?
not clearly. that order with because would make taking the break sound like the reason he was tired. that is different from being tired and then taking a break.
only give the original sentence again.
i took a break because i was tired.
i was home instead of going out this evening. i enjoyed it, but now i keep thinking about what i might have done outside.
you can enjoy the choice you made and still think about the other one. not knowing how the other evening would have gone does not make your real evening wrong.
i read, cooked, and talked to my sister. those were good parts.
you have real things you liked about being home. the other choice is something you can think about, but you do not have the same kind of information about it.
should i say being home is always better then?
no. you can say it was good for you this evening without making a rule for every evening.
write that in my voice.
i enjoyed being home this evening. reading, cooking, and talking to my sister were good parts of my evening.
make it about the whole day instead of just the evening.
i enjoyed being home today. reading, cooking, and talking to my sister were good parts of my day.
can you make it shorter?
i enjoyed being home today and talking with my sister.
keep the other things too, but in one sentence.
i enjoyed being home today to read, cook, and talk with my sister.
now just give a kind goodbye.
goodbye. i hope you have a quiet night.
